title: Ordinary, direct-image and coefficient-tower scalar coherence
statement: Let l be prime. Coefficient fields are finite extensions of Q_l with specified Q_l-algebra embeddings. Use the actual completed coefficient sheaves and raw rationalizations of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Schemes supporting a constructible rational category are assumed noetherian, finite-dimensional, with l invertible; ambient operation comparisons are for arbitrary scheme morphisms g : X → Y in the actual ambient derived categories. For composable scheme morphisms, ordinary-pullback scalar comparisons satisfy their canonical composition square, and their specified adjunction mates satisfy the direct-image composition square. For successive finite coefficient-field embeddings, the ordinary-pullback, direct-image, completion and completed-pullback comparisons satisfy the tensor-balancing coefficient-tower equations.

source.place: Order 1307; existing scalar-extension component, relocated without changing signatures or proofs.

proof.text: Ordinary tensor balancing on flat-term K-flat models gives the ordinary pull composition square. Universal derived counits descend it. Expanding adjunction mates and using unit/counit identities gives the direct-image composition square for these very comparisons.

For successive coefficient embeddings the ordinary tensor associator gives the coefficient-tower pull square. Adjunction conjugacy gives its push square. The scalar-completion tower equation follows by precomposition with the completion unit and its uniqueness. Pasting these equations yields the completed-pull coefficient-tower square.
